title: Finite discrete G-action realization
statement: Let K, Ks, and Omega be fields in Type u, with compatible algebra structures K → Ks → Omega, Ks a separable closure of K, and Omega algebraically closed. Set S = Spec K, J = its small etale topology, p = the point Spec Omega → S, G = Gal(Ks/K), and w = max(u,v). Let T : Sheaf J (Type w) → DiscreteContAction (Type w) G be a functor and j : U ∘ T ≅ p.sheafFiber a natural isomorphism, where U forgets the action. Assume the canonical germ formula of lem-exc-galois-stalk-action-functor: for each g, each extending K-automorphism tau of Omega, x' = Spec(tau) ≫ x, and section z, j(g • j⁻¹(germ_x z)) = germ_x' z. Then every M whose underlying set is finite is in T.essImage, namely there exists a sheaf F and an equivariant isomorphism T(F) ≅ M. This includes the empty finite set and arbitrary finite sets in Type w.

proof.text: Transport the finite underlying type of M to ULift (Fin n) in Type u. Conjugate the action by the resulting equivalence. The equivalence is a homeomorphism for the discrete topologies, so the transported action is continuous. Apply etaleFieldGsets and its counit to get an etale K-scheme X realizing this small action.

Construct F as the sheafification of the universe-lifted Yoneda presheaf of X. Its stalk is unchanged by sheafification by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheafification-geometric-stalk] (Point.presheafFiber.map toSheafify is an isomorphism). On the representable presheaf, evaluation sends a germ (Y,y,f) to y followed by f; the colimit relations give its well-definedness. Identity germs give its inverse, since every germ is represented by a section and toPresheafFiber_w identifies it with the identity germ at its image point. Thus identity germs identify the stalk with Omega-points. Precomposition with Spec(Ks -> Omega) is surjective by the existing separably-closed etale lift factorization theorem and injective by field-point precomposition injectivity. This identifies it with Ks-points.

Extend each g in Gal(Ks/K) to a K-automorphism tau of Omega. For a Ks-point y and its precomposition transform yprime under g, their Omega-points satisfy the change-of-lift equation because tau extends g. Apply the assumed germ formula to the image of the identity under the sheafification unit. Every stalk element is an identity germ, so the comparison through j is equivariant. Compose it with the inverse of points X from etaleFieldGsets, the counit isomorphism, and the finite-type transport. Action.mkIso and the two full-subcategory isoMk constructors give T(F) isomorphic to M. No nonemptiness assumption is used.
